2.6 Exercises

Exercise 2.6.1. Let \(C_0\) and \(C_1\) be categories and consider morphisms \(f_0\colon x_0 \to y_0\) and \(g_0\colon y_0 \to z_0\) in \(C_0\) and morphisms \(f_1\colon x_1 \to y_1\) and \(g_1\colon y_1 \to z_1\) in \(C_1\). Show that the composite \((g_0,g_1) \circ (f_0,f_1)\colon (x_0,x_1) \to (z_0,z_1)\) in \(C_0 \times C_1\) is given by \((g_0 \circ f_0, g_1 \circ f_1)\).
